s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin eruption with atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules on the buttocks
Atypical lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis with eosinophils and plasma cells
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
Eruption duration of 5 years
Previous treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy failed
History of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks
Syphilis screen results were negative
Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
Biopsy findings of dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes
Epidermotropism identified in second biopsy
Eosinophils and plasma cells present in the dermal infiltrate

raw.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
raw.rationale: The presence of a dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes, epidermotropism in the second biopsy, and a history of persistent eruption of 5 years' duration support this diagnosis. The lack of strong clonal rearrangement and negative syphilis screen also align with this condition.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: While mycosis fungoides is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, the absence of significant epidermotropism in the initial biopsy and the specific immunophenotype of CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes lean more towards Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes mycosis fungoides and other types of cutaneous T-cell lymphomas, but the specific characteristics of the case point more precisely to Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Lymphomatoid papulosis typically presents with more transient and self-healing lesions, which contrasts with the persistent eruption of 5 years in this case

rejected.label: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of atypical lymphocytes and the specific pattern of infiltration are more indicative of a lymphoma than a pseudolymphoma, which is often reactive and lacks atypia

gold: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma arising as Wolf's post-herpetic isotopic response
